alloys.alloys_notes: Main-element composition regimes reported: ferritic subgroup (<5 wt% Mn, very low C); duplex subgroup (5–30 wt% Mn, 5–10 wt% Al, 0.4–0.7 wt% C); austenitic subgroup (12–30 wt% Mn, 5–12 wt% Al, 0.6–1.2 wt% C). Microalloying elements Si, Cr, Cu, V, Nb, Mo, Ni are reviewed for κ-carbide control and strengthening; balance Fe.
alloys.description: A family of lightweight high-strength steels based on the Fe–Mn–Al–C system, about 18% lighter than conventional steels, exhibiting high strength and ductility through TRIP/TWIP/MBIP deformation mechanisms and κ-carbide strengthening; classified into ferritic, duplex, and austenitic groups depending on Mn and C content.

source.reason: The paper's entire subject is the Fe–Mn–Al–C lightweight steel system; the title and abstract name it, and the text classifies it into ferritic/duplex/austenitic groups with composition ranges.

paper.paper_scope: A review of the lightweight Fe–Mn–Al–C steel system, examining how the main alloying elements (Mn, Al, C) and microalloying additions (Si, Cr, Cu, V, Nb, Mo, Ni) influence phase distribution, κ-carbide formation and mechanical properties, and reviewing manufacturing/casting/rolling/heat-treatment routes, strengthening methods, and implementation challenges.
paper.title: Lightweight Fe–Mn–Al–C Steels: Current State, Manufacturing, and Implementation Prospects

processes.description: Melting and casting of Fe–Mn–Al–C steels using open induction furnaces or vacuum induction furnaces (also arc melting and centrifugal casting); the as-cast condition before subsequent deformation and heat treatment. Oxygen content usually below 6 ppm; olivine sand or preheated molds are used to minimize reactivity.
processes.processes_notes: Multiple casting routes are mentioned, including open induction, vacuum induction, arc melting, centrifugal casting, and laser powder bed fusion (LPBF).

processes.description: Solution treatment/austenitization at about 950–1050 °C followed by rapid cooling (e.g., water quenching) to dissolve residual carbides and fully austenitize the steel before aging.

processes.description: Aging at 500–700 °C for 0.5–2 h (or longer, e.g., 530 °C/538 °C for 10 h; about 550 °C) to nucleate nanodispersed κ-carbides and other strengthening precipitates.

processes.description: Annealing (intercritical or isothermal) at about 500–800 °C used to control κ-carbide distribution and phase balance; Al broadens the intercritical annealing temperature range.

unmapped_findings: This is a review paper that synthesizes results from many cited studies rather than reporting a single experimental campaign; therefore no discrete paper-level experimental samples (a specific alloy composition combined with a specific heat treatment and distinct sample label) are defined.

Numerous specific Fe–Mn–Al–C compositions are reviewed from the literature (e.g., Fe–30Mn–9Al–1C, Fe–28Mn–9Al–0.8C–3Cu, Fe–20Mn–9Al–3Cr–xC, Fe–30Mn–13.2Al–1.6C–5Cr); these are treated as examples within the single Fe–Mn–Al–C materials system rather than as separate paper-level alloys.
